title: Anansi and the Pot of Wisdom
subtitle: A tale explicitly set in Fanti-land

learningObjectives.text: What does Anansi do with all the wisdom?

pot.author: W. H. Barker and Cecilia Sinclair
pot.translator: not applicable; collected, arranged, and retold in English
pot.locator: Story II · HOW WISDOM BECAME THE PROPERTY OF THE HUMAN RACE; Story II · HOW WISDOM BECAME THE PROPERTY OF THE HUMAN RACE, normalized characters 53-2042
pot.excerpt: There once lived, in Fanti-land, a man named Father Anansi. He possessed all the wisdom in the world. People came to him daily for advice and help. One day the men of the country were unfortunate enough to offend Father Anansi, who immediately resolved to punish them. After much thought he decided that the severest penalty he could inflict would be to hide all his wisdom from them. He set to work at once to gather again all that he had already given. When he had succeeded, as he thought, in collecting it, he placed all in one great pot. This he carefully sealed, and determined to put it in a spot where no human being could reach it. Now, Father Anansi had a son, whose name was Kweku Tsin. This boy began to suspect his father of some secret design, so he made up his mind to watch carefully. Next day he saw his father quietly slip out of the house, with his precious pot hung round his neck. Kweku Tsin followed. Father Anansi went through the forest till he had left the village far behind. Then, selecting the highest and most inaccessible-looking tree, he began to climb. The heavy pot, hanging in front of him, made his ascent almost impossible. Again and again he tried to reach the top of the tree, where he intended to hang the pot. There, he thought, Wisdom would indeed be beyond the reach of every one but himself. He was unable, however, to carry out his desire. At each trial the pot swung in his way. For some time Kweku Tsin watched his father’s vain attempts. At last, unable to contain himself any longer, he cried out: “Father, why do you not hang the pot on your back? Then you could easily climb the tree.” Father Anansi turned and said: “I thought I had all the world’s wisdom in this pot. But I find you possess more than I do. All my wisdom was insufficient to show me what to do, yet you have been able to tell me.” In his anger he threw the pot down. It struck on a great rock and broke. The wisdom contained in it escaped and spread throughout the world.
pot.note: Verbatim text from Barker and Sinclair's 1917 English collection of Gold Coast stories. Attribute any specific community only where the collection does so.

narrativeBlocks.title: A pot for all the wisdom
narrativeBlocks.body: In Fanti-land they tell it: Anansi gathers all the wisdom in the world into one great pot — intending to hoard it and be the wisest being alive.

narrativeBlocks.title: The climb with the pot
narrativeBlocks.body: He ties the pot to his belly and starts climbing a tall tree to hide it at the top — but the pot in front makes the climb awkward, and he struggles up the trunk.

narrativeBlocks.title: The child's innocent correction
narrativeBlocks.body: His son, watching from below, calls out the obvious: 'Father, why not tie it on your back?' — a child's common sense out-thinking the keeper of all wisdom.

narrativeBlocks.title: The pot smashed on the ground
narrativeBlocks.body: In his rage at being out-thought by a child, Anansi throws the pot down — it smashes, and all the wisdom in it scatters into the world for anyone to pick up.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why wisdom is scattered
narrativeBlocks.body: That is why no one person has all the wisdom: it was smashed on the ground, and everyone got a little — the Akan explanation for distributed human wisdom.

quiz.prompt: What does Anansi intend to do with all the wisdom?

choices.text: Hoard it — gather it in one pot and hide it at the top of a tree

quiz.explanation: He means to keep it all — the hoarding instinct the tale is about.

quiz.prompt: Why is wisdom now scattered among all people?

choices.text: Anansi, angered at being out-thought by his own son, smashes the pot — and wisdom spreads to everyone
The pot melts in the sun
The pot is stolen by the monkey

quiz.explanation: The smash is the origin: wisdom is common property because of his rage.
